rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 6 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010): a real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence or cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype default; the real notification persists the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination as separate parties (repo-backend-p2-013) and sends each as its own party downstream (repo-tests-p3-204), so a template that copies the place of origin into every party would name the overseas place of origin as the GB consignee, importer and destination, which the prototype's shortcut cannot express; no DR1 judgement covers templates, and everywhere else the prototype still wins (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008).
outcome: A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, shows them on the template page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card as the design renders them, shows the consignee and consignor names on the template card, and seeds each back into a notification started from it; the contact address falls back to the place of origin where none was chosen, as the design does. The design's single copied address is set aside because the real notification persists and sends each party separately, a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
